deployments_detail.use: Marvell engineers/interns use AI coding tools as 'teammates' in software development, reporting cleaner code, faster issue resolution and better team alignment in fast-paced development work. [AI coding assistants (unspecified)]
Custom AI silicon (accelerators/CPUs) + optical interconnects/co-packaged optics for AI data centers

Marvell adopted Synopsys.ai Formal Advisor Copilot (generative AI) in its chip verification flow to automate property/assertion generation and assist engineers, reducing formal verification times and improving onboarding for new engineers. [Synopsys (Synopsys.ai Formal Advisor Copilot)]

Marvell uses the Synopsys.ai big-data / chip data analytics EDA tool to analyze the massive data generated during chip manufacturing and testing, improving process efficiency and quality and targeting reduced manufacturing/test costs. Greg Bazan (senior principal engineer) states the tool 'has been vital to improve the efficiency and quality of our manufacturing process.' [Synopsys (Synopsys.ai EDA Data Analytics)]

Marvell taps the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to power its AI-driven solutions, using Unity Catalog for centralized governance (quality, security, lineage) over secure, compliant and transparent data and AI workflows. [Databricks (Data Intelligence Platform, Unity Catalog)]

Marvell built an internal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system / custom LLM to assist chip designers with Verilog design and verification queries and early anomaly detection, streamlining the design/verification process (developed via Marvell's first GenAI intern program, exploring Copilot extensions). [Marvell internal (LLM/RAG; explored GitHub Copilot extensions)]

Marvell's advanced packaging platform for custom AI accelerators leverages NVIDIA machine learning models to shift testing from reactive to predictive, improving throughput, yield and overall quality. [NVIDIA (machine learning models)]

Marvell has adopted generative AI tools internally for employees and established a formal internal policy governing the usage of generative artificial intelligence tools across the company. [Internal generative AI tools (governance policy)]
